title: A central simple subalgebra makes the algebra a tensor product with its centralizer

standard_prerequisites.name: The degree formula for a centralizer
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that the degree of the algebra equals the product of the degrees of the subalgebra and of its centralizer, which gives the dimension equality used in the proof.

standard_prerequisites.name: Simplicity of the tensor product
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that the tensor product of the subalgebra with its centralizer is simple, so that the natural map into the algebra out of a simple algebra is injective.

core_obligations: The dimension equality (proof lines 791-792): the cited theorem on centralizers gives that the dimension of the algebra equals the dimension of the tensor product of the subalgebra with its centralizer.

The natural map (proof lines 793-796): the tensor product is simple by the cited lemma, so the natural multiplication map from it into the algebra has zero kernel and hence is injective, and an injective map between spaces of equal finite dimension is an isomorphism, which is the assertion.
proof_roadmap: Compare dimensions using the centralizer theorem.
Use simplicity of the tensor product to make the natural map injective.
Conclude that the map is an isomorphism.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a simple central subalgebra of a finite central simple algebra, the algebra is the tensor product of the subalgebra with its centralizer (statement lines 783-789). The proof is a complete argument: the centralizer theorem gives equality of the dimensions of the algebra and of that tensor product (proof lines 791-792), and simplicity of the tensor product makes the natural multiplication map injective, so that equality of dimensions upgrades injectivity to an isomorphism (proof lines 793-796). The non-formal content is the upgrade from injectivity to isomorphism by dimension. The claim is H2.
